name: Flights and boats into the Bangsamoro
note: Scheduled routes taken from airline, operator and government pages and dated reports, each with its source and the month it describes. Researched November 2026. Nothing here is a fare or a booking.

airports.name: Awang Airport
airports.note: Run by the Bangsamoro Airport Authority since 2023. Philippine Airlines is the only major airline with confirmed scheduled flights (Manila, Cebu, Tawi-Tawi).

airports.name: Sanga-Sanga Airport
airports.note: Jet service to Zamboanga on Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific, plus a PAL link to Cotabato. Run by the Bangsamoro Airport Authority.

airports.name: Jolo Airport
airports.note: Just outside the region: Sulu left BARMM after the Supreme Court ruling of 2024. Only small carriers fly here (Bangsamoro Airways, Leading Edge); Philippine Airlines has suspended its flights.

airports.name: Zamboanga International Airport
airports.note: Main gateway for the island provinces. Flights from Manila, Cebu, Davao and Iloilo, and the port next door has ferries to Basilan, Jolo and Bongao.

airports.name: Laguindingan Airport
airports.city: Laguindingan, Misamis Oriental (for Cagayan de Oro and Iligan)
airports.note: Nearest jet airport to Marawi and Lanao del Sur, with onward travel by road. Flights from Manila on Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific and AirAsia.

airports.name: Francisco Bangoy International Airport
airports.note: Large Mindanao hub with flights from Manila, Cebu and Clark. Buses run from Davao to Cotabato and Kabacan.

airports.name: General Santos International Airport
airports.note: Closed to commercial flights after the magnitude 7.8 earthquake on 8 June 2026 and reopened on 15 June 2026.

unverified: Cebu Pacific at Cotabato: Airportia lists 5J7286 Clark to Cotabato as weekly on Wednesdays, last seen 23 July 2026, but no airline or news source confirms it. FlyTeam's December 2025 Manila to Cotabato data lists only PAL. Cebu Pacific flew Manila to Cotabato (5J885 to 5J888) and Cebgo flew Zamboanga to Cotabato (DG6684/6685) in 2023. https://www.airportia.com/flights/5j7286/angeles-city/cotabato-city/

AirAsia Philippines at Zamboanga: a Malaya headline dated 16 September 2025, 'AirAsia expands operations in Zamboanga City', could not be opened (403) and may be an old 2022 story. A March 2026 Wikipedia snapshot lists Zamboanga as a terminated AirAsia destination (ended 2023). https://malaya.com.ph/business/corporate/airasia-expands-operations-in-zamboanga-city

PAL to Jolo: suspended 'in recent years', and the Bangsamoro Airport Authority said in August 2025 that it is working to restore the service. https://bangsamoro.gov.ph/news/latest-news/barmm-airport-authority-pushes-stronger-air-connectivity-security-in-sulu-amid-regional-shift/

Bangsamoro Airways expansion to Sibutu, Mapun, Basilan, General Santos and Kota Kinabalu was announced in April 2024. No evidence was found that any of these launched. https://bangsamoro.gov.ph/news/latest-news/new-airline-to-fly-across-barmm/

Other BARMM airports managed by the BAA (Wao and Malabang in Lanao del Sur, Mapun airstrip in Tawi-Tawi): no scheduled passenger service was found. https://portcalls.com/barmm-airport-authority-assumes-landside-operation-of-6-airports

International flights from Zamboanga or Tawi-Tawi: none confirmed operating in 2025 or 2026. Cebgo's 2017 Zamboanga to Sandakan flights and PAL's proposed Zamboanga to Kota Kinabalu service are historical, and a BIMP-EAGA item from November 2025 talks about reviving routes cut by the pandemic. https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1013002

Polloc Port (Parang, Maguindanao del Norte) to Lamitan RORO: MV Island Paradise, operated by SAFTI, launched daily service on 25 April 2023. No 2024 to 2026 confirmation was found that it still runs. The announced Lamitan to Jolo and Jolo to Bongao extensions are also unconfirmed. https://bangsamoro.gov.ph/news/latest-news/new-roro-route-to-ease-travel-between-cotabato-basilan/

A Polloc Port to Singapore shipping route was only at the discussion stage with RCL in February 2023 and is cargo-focused. https://motc.bangsamoro.gov.ph/motc-to-open-new-route-in-international-shipping

Adventurer Powercraft fast craft from Zamboanga to Jolo (about 2h 20m, ₱2,250) and Zamboanga to Isabela (45 minutes, ₱430): listed only on Pamasahe, with internally inconsistent times. No other source was found. https://pamasahe.com/routes/jolo-sulu-zamboanga-sug-adventurer-powercraft-schedule-fares

Aleson's Zamboanga to Jolo, Bongao and Siasi runs after the January 2026 fleet grounding: Pamasahe pages updated October 2026 still list them, but the only dated resumption notices (August and September 2026) cover Basilan, plus Sandakan in September 2026. https://pamasahe.com/posts/aleson-shipping-lines-resumes-daily-ferry-services-between-zamboanga-and-basilan

Daily Express (Sabah) story of 16 October 2026, 'Zamboanga-Sandakan ferry service resumes' (MV Antonia 1, Aleson): seen in search results only; the article URL could not be resolved. https://www.dailyexpress.com.my/local/?location=%27Sandakan%27
